description:
PRINCIPAL idea (2026-06-01): when the gauntlet DETECTS a critical issue (esp. a security bug / named threat), STOP + SURFACE to PRINCIPAL, then generate a DEDICATED dynamic workflow whose single explicit goal is to DEFEAT THAT SPECIFIC THREAT — rather than patching it inline as a sub-item of a larger arc.

WHY IT'S RIGHT (root-cause fit): origindex M2 failed because the security fix was a SUB-ITEM of a larger build (a ratification-grid bullet). Sub-goals drift — they compete with the 'real' deliverable, inherit the arc's framing, take the easier reading. Making threat-defeat the WHOLE GOAL of a dedicated workflow means it structurally cannot drift: the goal IS the threat, no larger deliverable to hide behind.

UNIFIES TONIGHT'S THREADS:
- Detection (Arc B / stoa--yfv .1/.2/.5/.6) = the TRIGGER (a named threat surfaced / a threat-coverage assertion failed).
- Dynamic workflows (stoa--04n workflow-composer) = the VEHICLE (goal-locked single-purpose orchestration).
- Threat-coverage assertion (stoa--yfv.1) = the workflow's SUCCESS CRITERION (passes ONLY if an EXECUTED probe drives the real attack path to blocked).
- 'Direction is scarce' thesis = the escalation logic (a security bug is a load-bearing human-attention moment; human confirms direction, agents execute remediation with goal locked).
- Closes external-review MAJOR-1 (false-confidence): goal=threat-defeat + pass-criterion=executed-attack-path-probe (not a writable sentence) means remediation can't pass on a plausible-but-false assertion.

WORKFLOW SHAPE (writes itself from shipped Arc A + Arc B disciplines): goal=block M<n> attack path. STRABO(map threat surface) -> DAEDALUS(mitigation + mandatory threat->mitigation map per op-disc §35.4) -> ARGUS(audit: does design defeat T?) -> HARD STOP -> ADA(build) -> VERA(threat-anchored probe, exercise the ACTUAL attack path per stoa--yfv.2) -> verdict MUST carry 'M defeats T via probe P' or structural FAIL (stoa--yfv.1).

THE HARD DESIGN QUESTION = trigger criteria (what's 'critical enough' to stop-the-world). HOOK: reuse Arc A's named-threat classification (op-disc §35.1, M<n>, ARGUS-confirmed, non-self-exemptable) — NOT a new fuzzy 'is this critical?' judgment. Trigger = a named threat surfaced-but-not-yet-defeated -> stop + surface + offer the remediation workflow.

POSITION: reframes Arc B (detection becomes 'detect -> escalate to remediation workflow', not just 'add inline checks'); bridges Arc B + stoa--04n (workflow-composer) + stoa--aox (discipline-enforcement). N=0 (design idea, not yet decided). Decide: fold into Arc B scope, or its own arc after stoa--04n lands the workflow-composer.
